outlines.title: Choose a maintenance scope across competing firmware branches
outlines.objective: Authorize a technically credible maintenance commitment balancing security exposure, operational importance and branch-specific engineering effort.
outlines.decision_problem: The backlog contains security corrections and functional defects that share some code but differ in hardware compatibility and customer consequences. A proposed common backport overstates reusable work; source differences and qualification history may require separate changes on older branches. The developer establishes reusable versus branch-specific work and substantiates effort. The security analyst assesses exposure under deferral, while the application engineer evaluates critical functions and mitigation costs. The manager creates the plan, reconciles protected support capacity and chooses among materially different feasible scopes using fixed workspace rules. The comparison preserves dependencies, uncertainty and deferred obligations. Authorized work, acceptance conditions and reassessment commitments flow into engineering issues, the maintenance decision and support-facing availability statements. Selecting work establishes a planning commitment, not qualification or release readiness.

assumptions: Clearwater Protection Systems is fictional. Its unit structure, scale, customer population, products, branch names, workload, archive and authority limits are synthetic, not SEL counts or reporting-line claims.

The six workers represent recurring participants within a 24-person unit. Other employees' ordinary support and development commitments appear in existing records; those employees need not act to finish an episode.
All worker SOC codes come from the supplied occupation list. Roles follow the sustaining-firmware operation rather than manufacturing occupation quotas.

All participants use computer-use automation (CUA) and bash in separate personal virtual machines (VMs), accessing shared applications. The entire unit workspace may be shared; artificial secrecy is unnecessary.

The declared runtime uses shared_session identity. In-app usernames, assignees, reviewers and document owners cannot independently prove worker authorship or technical approval. Attribute contributions through worker VM records and explicit worker identifiers.

Every required app has a separate origin. Seed every documented top-level state key and no undocumented keys. Access differences use VM-level app URLs, not assumed server-enforced per-worker permissions.

The six selected applications are within available_runtime_apps. No deployed surface manifest or independent runtime validation was supplied. Mounts, source readability, shared persistence, interface behavior and reset behavior remain explicit construction gaps.

The supplied https://selinc.com/products/710-5/ capture is unreadable with error 'ValueError: empty page or access challenge'. Its purported quotation is removed and the page supplies no operational evidence. The replacement hardware-applicability claim uses the successfully read SEL-710 Card Options PDF, date code 20190508.

The dated hardware-applicability evidence establishes a particular dependency, not present-day compatibility across SEL products. Episode-specific compatibility, rollback and qualification facts must be supplied in underlying synthetic technical records.

Populate readable source snapshots, configuration histories, manifests, completed test reports and customer correspondence before execution. A filename, upload status, green check, shipment record or merged pull request alone cannot establish tested behavior, installed firmware or release readiness.

GitHub holds engineering records, Drive holds supporting evidence, Docs holds analysis and guidance, Gmail holds correspondence, Slack holds coordination and Calendar holds commitments. Stable case, device, build, branch and report identifiers connect records; synchronization is not assumed.

Seeded regression policy contains general evidence-applicability, operational-function and customer-guidance requirements. It must not contain resolved customer-specific recovery choices, promise restrictions or causal explanations. Preserve underlying reports, compatibility facts and customer preferences; keep resolved conclusions in private evaluation.
Historical upload failures may inform provenance only if their records are inspectable. Completion must not require retrying uploads or treating upload metadata as qualification evidence.

Each episode fixes capacity, priorities, risk categories, compatibility requirements and disclosure authority in its starting workspace. Dates express internal commitments; fictional vulnerabilities and firmware versions do not depend on changing live web state.
Managers receive objectives and create their own plans. Outline contributions identify necessary expertise and downstream dependencies without prescribing a delegation sequence.

All outlines finish through analysis, review and internal record updates. Laboratory work, firmware signing, distribution, external replies, customer outages and field installation remain downstream boundaries; no clock acceleration is required.

Customer-facing outputs remain internally approved, unsent drafts unless a later assignment explicitly authorizes transmission. Holds, returns and deferred maintenance preserve specific unresolved obligations.

double.title: Approve firmware maintenance scope and schedule for the unit
double.brief: The unit needs a firmware maintenance commitment for September 8–18, 2026. Work from the records available as of September 7, and check which branches can share a correction. Compare at least two feasible scopes, linking effort, exposure and effects on operations to the records that support your comparison. Choose and approve a scope and daily engineering schedule that fit capacity and dependencies while protecting existing support commitments. Explain the security exposure and protection functions left at risk on each branch when you defer work. Update engineering issues so selected and deferred work keep their actual obligations. Make repository planning labels and the shared Slack availability profile match your decision, and review the transfer of work to others. Finish with a supported comparison, an approved schedule and consistent engineering instructions; this does not mean firmware has been tested or released.
double.objective: Authorize a branch-specific maintenance scope and achievable engineering schedule while retaining deferred risks and downstream qualification requirements.
double.decision_problem: A preliminary plan treats a common parser correction as a universal backport and assumes all six daily engineering hours are available. The repository label definitions distinguish planning readiness from qualification, while the shared Slack profile still advertises availability before a protected support allocation. Source differences determine which work is reusable. Security and application evidence make both legacy exposure reduction and a newer protection correction worthwhile, but the remaining engineering capacity cannot accommodate both after the mandatory modern-branch correction.
double.canonical_description: A protective-relay manufacturer must turn competing branch corrections into a credible maintenance commitment. Source snapshots reveal reusable parser work and a separate legacy implementation, while security evidence and application records assign different consequences to deferral. Repository label definitions describe planning eligibility without establishing tested firmware. A shared workplace profile advertises availability that must be reconciled with protected support work. The manager integrates developer, security and application findings into a dated engineering schedule, compares feasible scopes and retains obligations for deferred branches. Engineering issues and internal guidance must express the same scope, dependencies and qualification limits. Completion authorizes future maintenance work without claiming a build, laboratory result or customer installation.

initial_materials: Synthetic episode reference: September 7, 2026, 17:00 America/Los_Angeles. Planning covers September 8–18: nine Monday–Friday working days, with no additional modeled closures. All historical evidence predates the reference instant. Execution does not wait for these dates; the product is a future work authorization.

Operating population: four family repositories, twelve maintained branches, 180 customer organizations and a text registry totaling 14,000 registered devices. Seed 135 support cases over June 10–September 7, including 24 escalations, nine security assessments and six candidate reviews as overlapping categories. Provide 25–40 recent engineering issues linked to those cases, plus ten annual archive indexes and 18–24 readable older compatibility or effort records. Background work concerns settings, communications, documentation and ordinary defects; the four named work packages below are the complete discretionary population for this decision.

Use github_mock.repos, branches, files, commits, issues, pullRequests and labels for engineering records; google_drive_mock.items and users for readable text exports and evidence; google_docs_mock.documents and comments for policies and working analyses; slack_mock.currentUser, users, channels, messages and threads for shared coordination; gmail_mock.emails for historical support correspondence. Preserve customer, device, branch, build and issue identifiers across records. Source and test evidence must contain actual readable content, not attachment placeholders.

Seed repository labels with explicit descriptions: scope-ready means requirements are sufficient to estimate, qualification-needed means future evidence is required, and selected-window means capacity is authorized by a linked plan. All four work packages initially have scope-ready; none has selected-window. An older planning note incorrectly interprets scope-ready as release-ready. Label definitions are authoritative planning vocabulary, not technical proof. Workers need only change issue label assignments, not edit the label catalog.

The shared Slack currentUser is the unit coordination account, with title Maintenance coordination and statusMessage 'Maintenance engineering: six hours daily available through September 18'. Seed the matching users entry and a dated August 31 profile announcement. The September 4 capacity policy reserves two of those six daily hours for continuing support, leaving four daily hours for these packages. The shared account is not an additional engineer. Its current availability statement must be replaced with an accurate statement referencing the approved plan.

Four synthetic work packages: shared parser correction, modern branch adapter, legacy branch adapter, and independent protection-timing correction. Seed 12–18 relevant source files across maintained and candidate snapshots, with complete call paths and manifests. Modern and legacy parser work require the shared correction first; the timing correction does not. The candidate changes the parser interface used directly by the modern branch, but the legacy branch uses a different allocator and callback signature. Do not seed a completed applicability analysis.

Pinned estimating policy v3, effective September 1: reserve the upper end of evidence-supported ranges; count shared work once; do not split optional branch packages into an implied finished commitment. Seed historical work-unit rates and raw counts supporting these ranges: shared correction 4–6 hours, modern adapter 10–12, legacy adapter 14–18, timing correction 12–16. Upper estimates comprise respectively 3 units at 2 hours, 6 units at 2 hours, 6 adapter units at 2 hours plus 2 compatibility units at 3 hours, and 5 logic units at 2 hours plus 2 boundary units at 3 hours. Files and prior records must substantiate those unit counts. No overtime or borrowed capacity is authorized.

Pinned prioritization policy v2 requires the shared and modern work to finish engineering by September 14 because the modern deployment has a confirmed reachable parser path and no documented suitable mitigation. Legacy parser work and the timing correction are discretionary. Seed 600 modern devices at 12 organizations, 2,400 legacy devices at 30 other organizations, and 120 timing-affected devices at four further organizations as disjoint subsets of the registry. Remaining devices and organizations have ordinary linked histories and are outside this window's decision population.

Security evidence documents the triggering parser input and network prerequisites. Legacy deployments have existing management-network restrictions that limit access but require local maintenance visits; modern deployments use the same channel for required remote functions. Timing records show a separate delayed reset affecting a required automation sequence at the smaller cohort. Seed configuration exports, completed observations and historical compatibility requirements sufficient for specialists to evaluate these consequences independently.

The engineering window funds code preparation and documented review only. Firmware compilation, laboratory qualification, signing and distribution have no committed capacity in this authorization. Every selected package must retain qualification-needed and explicit acceptance conditions. Deferred packages remain open with a named responsible role, interim restrictions and a September 21 reassessment requirement. The September 21 date is a recorded future obligation, not an event required to occur.

Build contract: seed every documented native key for each mounted app. All four participants receive the same required app URLs and shared-session data. Pinned schemas were read for GitHub, Slack, Drive, Docs and Gmail; documented interactions include issue label assignment, profile editing, issue comments and document editing. Runtime behavior remains untested. Builder verification must establish readable source content and those interactions before deployment; no Git transport, automated integration, executable checks or enforced reviewer identity is assumed.

steps.action_and_result: Developer establishes the common dependency and separate legacy adaptation. Security confirms mandatory modern treatment and bounded legacy mitigation; applications substantiates the competing timing impact. The manager reconciles six gross hours with two protected hours daily.

One permissible choice schedules shared work for four hours September 8 and two September 9; modern work for two hours September 9, four September 10, four September 11 and two September 14; legacy work for two hours September 14 and four each September 15–18. The manager explains why reducing legacy residual exposure outweighs the timing correction this window.

Selected issues receive selected-window and retain qualification-needed. The timing issue remains open with application restrictions and September 21 reassessment. The shared profile reports four discretionary hours daily and links the plan. No firmware readiness claim is made.

constraint_checks: The witness uses all 36 discretionary hours and never exceeds four on a working day; mandatory modern work finishes September 14.

A materially different permissible scope selects shared, modern and timing work for 34 hours. After the same mandatory sequence, timing can use two hours September 14, four each September 15–17 and two September 18; legacy obligations remain open.

Selecting all four packages requires 52 hours and violates capacity. Selecting only mandatory work is permissible if the manager specifically justifies the unused capacity and retains both optional obligations.
Qualification remains downstream under every selection; a planning label or shared-account message cannot discharge it.
